title: Our bodies are God’s temple
source_text: Εἰ δὲ καὶ ναοὺς ναοῖς δεῖ παραβαλεῖν, ἵνα παραστήσωμεν τοῖς ἀποδεχομένοις τὰ Κέλσου ὅτι νεὼς μὲν ἱδρύεσθαι τοὺς πρέποντας τοῖς εἰρημένοις ἀγάλμασι καὶ βωμοῖς οὐ φεύγομεν, ἐκτρεπόμεθα δὲ τῷ πάσης ζωῆς χορηγῷ ἀψύχους καὶ νεκροὺς οἰκοδομεῖν νεώς· ἀκουέτω ὁ βουλόμενος, τίνα τρόπον διδασκόμεθα ὅτι τὰ σώματα ἡμῶν „ναὸς τοῦ θεοῦ“ ἐστι, καὶ „εἴ τις“ διὰ τῆς ἀκολασίας ἢ τῆς ἁμαρτίας „φθείρει“ „τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ,“ οὗτος ὡς ἀληθῶς ἀσεβὴς εἰς τὸν ἀληθῆ ναὸν φθαρήσεται. πάντων δὲ τῶν οὕτως ὀνομαζομένων ναῶν κρείττων ἦν καὶ διαφέρων νεὼς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ καθαρὸν σῶμα τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ, ὅστις ἐπιστάμενος ἐπιβουλεύεσθαι μὲν δύνασθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀσεβῶν τὸν ναὸν τοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ θεοῦ, οὐ μὴν ὥστε ἰσχυροτέραν εἶναι τὴν τῶν ἐπιβουλευόντων προαίρεσιν τῆς τὸν νεὼν οἰκοδομούσης θειότητος, φησὶ πρὸς ἐκείνους· „λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον, κἀγὼ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν.“ τοῦτο δὲ „ἔλεγε περὶ τοῦ ναοῦ τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ.“ καὶ ἄλλως δὲ οἱ θεῖοι λόγοι τὰ περὶ ἀναστάσεως μυστικῶς διδάσκοντες τοὺς δυναμένους ἀκούειν θειοτέρᾳ ἀκοῇ λόγων θεοῦ, ἀνοικοδομηθήσεσθαί (φασι) λίθοις ζῶσι καὶ τιμιωτάτοις· αἰνιττόμενοι ὅτι ἕκαστος τῶν συμπνεόντων διὰ τοῦ αὐτοῦ λόγου εἰς τὴν κατ᾿ αὐτὸν εὐσέβειαν λίθος ἐστὶ τίμιος τοῦ παντὸς ναοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ. καθὸ ὑπὸ μὲν τοῦ Πέτρου λέγεται· „ὑμεῖς δὲ οἰκοδομεῖσθε λίθοι ζῶντες καὶ οἶκος πνευματικὸς εἰς ἱεράτευμα ἅγιον, ἀνενέγκαι πνευματικὰς θυσίας εὐπροσδέκτους θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,“ ὑπὸ δὲ τοῦ Παύλου τό· „οἰκοδομηθέντες ἐπὶ τῷ θεμελίῳ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ προφητῶν. ὄντος ἀκρογωνιαίου λίθου αὐτοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.“ τοιοῦτον δέ τινα μυστικὸν ἔχει νοῦν καὶ ἡ ἐν τῷ Ἡσαΐᾳ λέξις. οὕτως ἔχουσα καὶ λεγομένη ὡς πρὸς τὴν Ἱερουσαλήμ· „ἰδοὺ ἑτοιμάζω σοι ἄνθρακα τὸν λίθον σου καὶ τὰ θεμέλιά σου σάπφειρον, καὶ θήσω τὰς ἐπάλξεις σου ἴασπιν καὶ τὰς πύλας σου λίθους κρυστάλλου καὶ τὸν περίβολόν σου λίθους ἐκλεκτοὺς, καὶ πάντας τοὺς υἱούς σου διδακτοὺς θεοῦ· καὶ ἐν πολλῇ εἰρήνῃ τὰ τέκνα σου, καὶ ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ οἰκοδομηθήσῃ.“
pass_a_gloss: And if it is needed to set temples (ναοί) beside (παραβάλλω) temples, so that we may present (παρίστημι) to those accepting (ἀποδέχομαι) the things of Celsus that we do not flee (φεύγω) setting up temples (νεῴ) fitting (πρέπω) to the said statues and altars, but we turn aside (ἐκτρέπομαι) from building (οἰκοδομέω) for the supplier (χορηγός) of all life (ζωή) soulless (ἄψυχος) and dead (νεκρός) temples: let the one wishing hear in what manner we are taught that our bodies (σώματα) are temple of God, and if anyone through licentiousness (ἀκολασία) or sin (ἁμαρτία) destroys (φθείρω) the temple of God, this one, as truly impious (ἀσεβής) toward the true temple, will be destroyed. And better (κρείττων) and differing (διαφέρω) than all the temples so named was the temple, the holy (ἱερός) and pure (καθαρός) body of our Saviour Jesus, who, knowing (ἐπίσταμαι) that the temple of the God in him could be plotted against (ἐπιβουλεύω) by the impious, not however so that the choice/purpose (προαίρεσις) of the plotters be stronger than the divinity (θειότης) building the temple, says to them: loose/destroy (λύω) this temple, and I in three days will raise (ἐγείρω) it. And this he was saying about the temple of his body. And otherwise also the divine words (θεῖοι λόγοι), teaching mystically (μυστικῶς) the things concerning resurrection (ἀνάστασις) to those able to hear with a more divine hearing (ἀκοή) of words of God, [say] it will be rebuilt (ἀνοικοδομέω) with living (ζῶντες) and most precious (τιμιώτατοι) stones (λίθοι), hinting (αἰνίττομαι) that each of those breathing together (συμπνέω) through the same word/Word into the piety (εὐσέβεια) according to him is a precious stone of the whole temple of God; according as it is said by Peter: you are being built (οἰκοδομέω) living stones and a spiritual (πνευματικός) house (οἶκος) for a holy priesthood (ἱεράτευμα), to offer up (ἀναφέρω) spiritual sacrifices (θυσίαι) well-acceptable (εὐπρόσδεκτος) to God through Jesus Christ; and by Paul the: having been built on the foundation (θεμέλιον) of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus our Lord himself being cornerstone (ἀκρογωνιαῖος) stone. And the wording (λέξις) in Isaiah also has some such mystical sense (νοῦς), being thus and spoken as to Jerusalem: behold I prepare (ἑτοιμάζω) for you carbuncle (ἄνθραξ) your stone and your foundations sapphire (σάπφειρος), and I will set your battlements (ἐπάλξεις) jasper (ἴασπις) and your gates stones of crystal (κρύσταλλος) and your enclosure (περίβολος) chosen (ἐκλεκτοί) stones, and all your sons taught (διδακτοί) of God, and in much peace (εἰρήνη) your children, and in righteousness you will be built.
pass_b_english: If temples too must be set beside temples, so that we may show those who accept Celsus’s views that we do not shun setting up temples fit for the statues and altars we have described, but that we turn away from building lifeless and dead temples to the Giver of all life, let anyone who wishes hear how we are taught that our bodies are “a temple of God” (1 Corinthians 3:16; 1 Corinthians 6:19), and that “if anyone,” through licentiousness or sin, “destroys the temple of God” (1 Corinthians 3:17), he, as one truly impious toward the true temple, will be destroyed.

But the temple better and more excellent than all those so named was the holy and pure body of our Saviour Jesus. He knew that the temple of the God within him could be plotted against by the impious, yet not in such a way that the purpose of the plotters would be stronger than the Godhead that built the temple. So he says to them: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up” (John 2:19). And this “he was saying about the temple of his body” (John 2:21).

In another way, too, the divine Scriptures teach in a hidden sense what concerns the resurrection to those who can hear the words of God with a more divine hearing. They say that the temple will be built again with living and most precious stones, hinting that each of those who are of one spirit, through the same Word, in the piety that accords with him is a precious stone of the whole temple of God. So Peter says: “You are being built up, living stones and a spiritual house, for a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ” (1 Peter 2:5); and Paul: “built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus our Lord himself being the cornerstone” (Ephesians 2:20).

The passage in Isaiah, too, has some such hidden meaning. It reads as follows, addressed to Jerusalem: “Behold, I am preparing for you carbuncle as your stone, and sapphire as your foundations; and I will make your battlements of jasper, and your gates of crystal stones, and your outer wall of choice stones; and all your sons taught by God, and your children in great peace; and in righteousness you shall be built” (Isaiah 54:11–14).

choices.choice: ‘Our bodies are a temple of God’ combines 1 Corinthians 3:16 (‘you are God’s temple’) and 6:19 (‘your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit’). In 1 Corinthians 3:17 Paul says ‘God will destroy him’; Origen’s sentence has the passive ‘will be destroyed’, rendered as he gives it. ἐκτρεπόμεθα is rendered ‘we turn away from’, not the stronger ‘refuse’. ‘The temple of the God within him’ renders τὸν ναὸν τοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ θεοῦ. φασι in ‘They say that the temple will be built again’ is an editorial supplement and is accepted; the subject ‘the temple’ is understood from the context. ‘Of one spirit’ renders συμπνεόντων (‘breathing together’); διὰ τοῦ αὐτοῦ λόγου is capitalised as the Word, though ‘the same teaching’ is possible. Origen’s 1 Peter 2:5 begins ὑμεῖς δὲ οἰκοδομεῖσθε λίθοι ζῶντες where the New Testament has καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡς λίθοι ζῶντες οἰκοδομεῖσθε; his form has no ‘as’, so ‘living stones’ stands in apposition. His Ephesians 2:20 adds λίθου and τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν; both are translated as he quotes them. ὡς πρὸς τὴν Ἱερουσαλήμ is rendered ‘addressed to Jerusalem’ (the oracle is spoken to her, not ‘as if’). Isaiah 54:11-14 follows the Septuagint wording, which differs from the Hebrew; its clauses about the sons and children have no verb in the Greek and are left so; ἄνθραξ is rendered ‘carbuncle’ (a deep red gem).
